items.wrong: He said me that he was coming.
items.fix: He told me that he was coming.
items.why: Use told me ou said sem me.

items.wrong: She said that she is tired yesterday.
items.fix: She said that she was tired.
items.why: No relato, o verbo vai para o passado.

items.wrong: This is more good than that.
items.why: O comparativo de good é better.

teach.goal: Como não traduzir palavra por palavra.
solo: Pergunte por que o erro acontece em português e como evitar.
group: Compare erro e forma natural: He said me that he was coming. → He told me that he was coming. | She said that she is tired yesterday. → She said that she was tired. | This is more good than that. → This is better than that..
Peça que digam a forma natural em voz alta.
extra90: Cada aluno cria um erro típico seu e o grupo corrige.

facts.big: He said that… / used to / bigger than
facts.label: Revisão do jantar
facts.sub: Use said/told + that + passado para relatar, used to para hábitos antigos e os comparativos (bigger than, the best) para comparar pessoas e coisas.

facts.label: Ele disse que…
facts.sub: Use said that ou told me that e mova o verbo para o passado: My uncle said that he was bringing his family. She said that her grandmother’s dish is older than the house.

facts.label: Costumava
facts.sub: Use used to + verbo base para um hábito do passado: She used to cook for twenty people. No negativo e na pergunta, use use to: Did she use to cook alone?

paragraphs: It is a cold Thursday evening in Boston, and the windows are warm with light. Emma comes into the dining room with a bottle of juice. Her friend Clara puts a napkin next to every plate. Her cousins sit on the sofa and talk loudly. Every guest brings something to eat. Emma is happy to be part of this family.

“Clara, this table is bigger than last year’s. Who is coming?” says Emma. “My uncle called and said that he was bringing his family.” says Clara. “Wonderful! Did your grandmother use to cook all this by herself?” says Emma.
